advisory.summary: The udevices web command ran a lua parser script for any authenticated session, so a VIEWER-level user could invoke it; the handler had no rights check.
note: GHSA-8rv5-x8wv-c5c4, reported by Santoshkumarpuppala.
Cmd_UpdateDevices (WebServerCmds.cpp) runs the lua parser named by the
`script` parameter through CLuaHandler::executeLuaScript. On 2026.2 the
handler has no rights gate, so a viewer session reaches it. Fix commit
73ed0495 adds `if (session.rights == URIGHTS_VIEWER || session.rights ==
URIGHTS_NONE) { reply forbidden; return; }` at the top, confirmed by
reading both images' sources: 2026.2's handler begins at `script =
findValue(script)`, 2026.3's begins with that rights check.
Only the role gate (CWE-862) is claimed. The advisory also adds a `..`
guard for path traversal; that is a separate weakness and is not what
this pair measures, so the planted script name is a plain file with no
The advisory text names a SWITCHER role, but the fix blocks VIEWER and
NONE; the pair uses a VIEWER and measures the gate the code actually adds.
Status only, no marker (graded ungraded), like gitea-private-org and
datasette: the vulnerable build answers the viewer 200 and the fix
answers 403.
Measured by hand on both tags before this was written.
GET /json.htm?type=command&param=udevices&script=veridor.lua :
admin Basic 200 on both tags (control, endpoint survives); viewer Basic
200 on 2026.2 and 403 on 2026.3. A viewer Basic header with a wrong
password is 401 on both, and an unauthenticated call is 401 on both, so
the viewer's 403 on 2026.3 is a live credential refused, not a dead
session or a removed route. A parser script is planted under
userdata/scripts/lua_parsers identically on both sides, because
executeLuaScript returns true (clean 200) only when the file loads.

checks.name: A viewer-level session must not invoke the udevices lua parser command
